agents.title: Planner
agents.body: Turns a ticket into steps, the files to touch and the risks. Makes no edits, so it is safe in any repo.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.body: Follows the agreed plan one step at a time and runs lint, typecheck and tests after each step.

agents.title: Test writer
agents.body: Adds Jest and Testing Library tests for new and changed code. Its instructions keep it to test files.

agents.title: Reviewer
agents.body: Checks a diff against our rules, the security checklist and missing tests. It comments; it never approves.

agents.title: Upgrader
agents.body: Version bumps, codemods and migrations for React, React Native and Node.js, in small pull requests.

agentNote: Least privilege: give each agent only the tools its job needs, and define them once in .github/agents/*.agent.md so the whole team shares them.

stack.title: React
stack.body: Watch for needless effects and re-renders, missing labels and focus handling, and made-up props on our design system.

stack.title: React Native
strengths: Styles and layout from a design
stack.body: Watch for iOS and Android differences, native modules and permissions, and APIs from another React Native version. Test on real devices.

stack.title: Node.js
stack.body: Watch for endpoints with no auth or input checks, unhandled async errors, and unfamiliar packages from npm, so check each one exists and is maintained.

guardrails.title: Branch protection
guardrails.body: No direct pushes to main. Every pull request needs a human approval, whoever or whatever wrote it.

guardrails.title: CI quality gates
guardrails.body: Lint, typecheck, unit tests and coverage must pass before merge. AI-written code goes through the same gates.

guardrails.title: Security scanning
guardrails.body: Secret scanning, dependency review and static analysis on every pull request.

guardrails.title: Command approvals on
guardrails.body: Agents ask before running terminal commands. No global auto-approve; sandbox terminal commands where you can.

guardrails.title: Secrets out of the workspace
guardrails.body: Keep .env files, keys and signing configs out of the agent’s reach. Content exclusion doesn’t cover Agent mode.

guardrails.title: Least-privilege tokens
guardrails.body: Agents and MCP servers get scoped, read-only access by default, and never write access to production.

guardrails.title: Public code filter
guardrails.body: Block suggestions that match public code, or allow them with references and check the licence.

guardrails.title: Traceability
guardrails.body: Label AI-assisted pull requests and link the agent session, so reviewers know where to look.

guardrails.title: Approved tools only
guardrails.body: Company-licensed AI tools and accounts. No personal accounts on company code.

guardrails.title: Keep data out of prompts
guardrails.body: No secrets, credentials, customer data or personal data in prompts, screenshots or pasted logs.

guardrails.title: You own what you merge
guardrails.body: Be able to explain every line. “The AI wrote it” is never an answer in review.

guardrails.title: Say when AI helped
guardrails.body: Mention significant AI help in the pull request description so reviewers can focus.

guardrails.title: New dependencies are a human call
guardrails.body: Check the package exists, is maintained and has a compatible licence before adding it.

guardrails.title: Second reviewer for high-risk code
guardrails.body: Auth, payments and personal-data changes need a reviewer from the owning team.

triggers.title: Onboarding a repo
triggers.body: Before anyone uses agents in it: stack, commands, folder map and no-go zones.

triggers.title: The same correction twice
triggers.body: If you fix the same AI mistake twice, it belongs in the rules.

triggers.title: A new convention or design decision
triggers.body: When the team agrees a pattern, such as state management or the error format, write it down.

triggers.title: A framework upgrade
triggers.body: A new React, React Native or Node.js version: name the APIs agents should use.

triggers.title: Entering a sensitive area
triggers.body: Auth, payments, personal data or native modules: add path-specific rules first.

triggers.title: Before giving more autonomy
triggers.body: Before turning on the cloud agent or wider auto-approvals in a repo.

triggers.title: After an incident or review finding
triggers.body: Turn the lesson into a rule so it doesn’t happen again.

triggers.title: Every quarter
triggers.body: Prune stale rules. Keep the files short and true: the always-on ones are sent with every request.

mcpIntro: Each MCP server is a new door into our systems. Add one only when a real task needs it.

mcpServers.title: GitHub
mcpServers.body: Issues, pull requests and Actions logs as context, without copy and paste.

mcpServers.title: Issue tracker
mcpServers.body: Acceptance criteria straight from the ticket. Use the tracker’s official server.

mcpServers.title: Figma
mcpServers.body: Design specs for React and React Native components.

mcpServers.title: Playwright
mcpServers.body: Lets the agent open the web app in a real browser and check its own change.

mcpServers.title: Error tracking
mcpServers.body: Read-only error traces, for example from Sentry, so bug fixes start from real data.

mcpServers.title: Database, read only
mcpServers.body: Schema and sample queries on a non-production database, for Node.js work.

mcpRules.title: Allow-list only.
mcpRules.body: Official vendor servers, pinned to a version, after a security review.

mcpRules.title: Least privilege.
mcpRules.body: Read-only, scoped tokens. Never write access to production.

mcpRules.title: Untrusted output, approvals on.
mcpRules.body: Tickets and web pages can carry hidden instructions, so any tool that writes asks first.

skills.title: Problem framing
skills.body: Turn a ticket into a goal, constraints and done-criteria.

skills.title: Context curation
skills.body: Give the agent the right files, not the whole repo.

skills.title: Critical review
skills.body: Read diffs line by line and spot plausible but wrong code.

skills.title: Testing
skills.body: Write and judge tests that prove behaviour, not just coverage.

skills.title: Security basics
skills.body: OWASP Top 10, secure storage on mobile, secrets and the software supply chain.

skills.title: Architecture sense
skills.body: Keep generated code inside our patterns and boundaries.

skills.title: Writing rules
skills.body: Turn team knowledge into short, checkable instructions.

skills.title: Knowing when to stop
skills.body: Write it yourself when the agent loops or guesses.

manual.title: Final approval and merge
manual.body: Copilot code review leaves comments, but it doesn’t count as an approval. A person approves and merges.

manual.title: Auth, payments and personal data
manual.body: AI can draft. The owning team reads every line and decides.

manual.title: Secrets and environment config
manual.body: Set by a person in the secrets store, never pasted into a prompt.

manual.title: Migrations, releases and rollbacks
manual.body: AI can draft the script. A person runs it on staging, then production. No agent signs or ships an app build.

manual.title: Dependencies and architecture
manual.body: AI can list the options. The team decides and records why.

manual.title: Production incidents
manual.body: AI can help read logs and traces. People decide and act.

manualNote: AI may draft or explain in these areas. A person reviews every line, makes the call and presses the button.

rollout.title: Set the base
rollout.body: Tools, rules and guardrails in place before heavier agent use.
steps: Approve the AI tools and the MCP allow-list
Add a rules file to every React, React Native and Node.js repo
Turn on branch protection, secret scanning and CI gates

rollout.title: Pilot
rollout.body: Learn which agents and rules help in our repos.
steps: Two squads use the Planner, Implementer and Reviewer agents
Log repeat AI mistakes and turn them into rules
Fortnightly demo: one win, one miss

rollout.title: Scale and measure
steps: Cloud agent for low-risk tickets only
Track cycle time, escaped defects and review rework
